1 شَقِذَ , aor.
شَقَذَ , (S, M, L, K,) inf. n. شَقَذٌ, (S, M, L,) He scarcely ever, or never, slept, and had a malignant eye, affecting, or hurting, others, therewith: (S, M, L, K: *) or he had a strong, or powerful, eye, quickly affecting or hurting [others therewith]. (M, L, K.) ―
-b2- And شَقِذَ, (S, M, L, K,) aor.
شَقَذَ ; (K;) and شَقَذَ, aor.
شَقِذَ ; (L, K;) He went away, (S, M, L, K,) and went far off, (S, L,) being driven away. (S, L, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
